title: Ops sprint weeknote: queue sampling and cache priorities
body:
Date: 2029-03-11 to 2029-03-13
Owners: Ethan Liu (lead), Maya Chen (experiments), Carlos Rivera (infra), Priya Natarajan (kernel)
Attendees: eng-serving-runtime, oncall SRE (Liam), product-observability (Anika)

TL;DR:
- Rolled out queue-sampler v0.3 to shadow for dev region; initial results show 7–11% reduction in tail latency on small-sequence requests without hurting throughput.
- Experimented with a two-tier cache-priority score (shadow-warmth + request-cohort) and observed 4% fewer cold reads for chat-like workloads.
- Kernel team landed a lightweight cooperative-yield patch to avoid busy-spin during microbatch boundary, reduced CPU steal incidents in the VM hosts.

Progress this week (concise):
- Queue-sampling experiment: shadow rollout -> collect metrics -> quick analysis -> decision to expand. (Maya)
- Cache-priority prototype: implemented scoring and eviction hook; test harness validated in perfbench. (Carlos)
- Kernel yield patch: merged to canary branch; monitoring enabled. (Priya)
- Incident followup: two small infra CPU-throttle events tied to prefetch storms; mitigation script added to autoscaler. (Liam)

Key metrics (dev shadow vs baseline, 48h window):
- p50 token latency: baseline 12.8ms -> shadow 12.6ms (1.6% improvement)
- p95 token latency: baseline 36.2ms -> shadow 33.7ms (7% improvement)
- p99 token latency: baseline 92ms -> shadow 86.1ms (6.5% improvement)
- CPU utilization (inference host): +1.5% avg; kernel CPU steal events down 42% after yield patch
- Cold cache misses per 1k requests: baseline 42 -> prototype 40 (4.7% improvement)

Observations / qualitative notes:
- The queue-sampler prioritizes short jobs differently than the old FIFO window and reduces head-of-line blocking for 1–3 token prompts. Effects are most visible during medium concurrency (50–150 req/s) bursts.
- Shadow-warmth scoring (recent-hit-weight + TTL-age-bonus) helps keep conversational KV entries warm for multi-turn flows. Tuning the age bonus to 0.6 gave best tradeoff in tests.
- Kernel cooperative-yield reduced busy loops at microbatch flush boundaries; observed fewer syscalls per second spikes which previously correlated with host preemption.

Experiment log (repro notes):
- queue-sampler v0.3 (feature flags: sampler=true, sampler_mode=shadow-v3)
- sampling policy: weighted-random by estimated-latency-sensitivity, with FIFO fallback at >500ms queue depth
- test harness: ./tools/perfbench --scenario=chat-mixed --qps=120 --duration=2h --seed=73
- results stored in S3: s3://redwood-results/queue-sampler/2029-03-11/run-73-agg.json
- cache-priority test: feature flag cache_priority=alpha, age_bonus=0.6, warmth_decay=0.85

Notable tradeoffs: 
- Slightly higher average CPU due to additional sampler bookkeeping (per-request metadata). Worth it for reductions in p99.
- Cache-priority increases churn in small-key hotsets; we observed increased eviction churn for short-lived ephemeral keys (alerts added).

Incidents / bugs surfaced:
- #INC-5682: autoscaler mis-saw prefetch storms as sustained load; temporary script added: autoscaler-guard.sh (low-risk) to threshold on 10m median qps.
- #BUG-1221: sampler occasionally misclassifies long-context requests when trailing tokens are short; root cause: context-length estimator edge-case. Patch queued in PR #2441.

Decisions made during sync:
- Expand queue-sampler shadow to staging across all regions next week if reduced p99 holds for 72h. (Decision: consensus)
- Keep cache-priority alpha in dev-only for one more week; instrument more fine-grained eviction telemetry before wider rollout.
- Build a small kernel telemetry exporter to track busy-loop counters and batch-flush syscall spikes. (Priya to lead)

Action items (owner / due):
- Maya: run extended 7-day shadow run in staging for queue-sampler and produce expanded report (due 2029-03-20)
- Carlos: add eviction-churn alert (pager) for ephemeral-key surge and roll to canary infra (due 2029-03-15)
- Priya: land kernel telemetry exporter + dashboard and wire to incident runbooks (due 2029-03-18)
- Ethan: coordinate product-observability meeting to define SLO delta threshold for sampler rollouts (due 2029-03-16)
- Liam: tune autoscaler-guard.sh thresholds and evaluate false-positive rate (due 2029-03-14)

Notes for next sync / talking points:
- Can we formalize an acceptance criteria matrix for sampler-induced overhead vs p99 improvement? (proposal: <=3% avg CPU uplift and >=5% p99 reduction to proceed)
- Discuss budget/seat impact if sampler improves tail (product asks for expected cost delta).
- Kernel: do we push yield patch to prod canary or hold for telemetry dashboard first?

Appendix: quick CLI snippets
- enable shadow sampling on a node: rdctl feature-set sampler=true sampler_mode=shadow-v3 --node node-17
- dump sampler stats: rdctl debug sampler-stats --since 1h --json > /tmp/sampler-stats.json
- test harness command (repro): ./tools/perfbench --scenario=chat-mixed --qps=120 --duration=2h --seed=73

Open questions / parking lot:
- Should the sampler expose per-tenant knobs or remain service-wide? (defer to next sprint; product wants per-tenant opt-in)
- Evaluate long-term effect of cache-priority on multi-tenant noisy neighbor scenarios.

End of weeknote. Leaving some raw metrics and query traces in the linked S3 bucket for anyone wanting to poke.
